overclaims: OpenAI's technical report expressly withheld detailed architecture and training-dataset information, and the contemporaneous filing accurately identified those omissions.
checks.note: The statement excerpt, proposition, axis and outcome are all fine. Problems: (1) The rationale says the technical report 'expressly withheld' details and that the filing was 'accurate'. That rests on Section 2 text, which is not in e2's quoted words or context. e2 only quotes the abstract's Transformer line. (2) The public citation excerpts are cut to fragments ('OpenAI', 'Transformer-based model'), so they don't show the evidence. (3) The packet lists e2 as material counterevidence, and its quoted line qualifies the claim, yet it is published as 'supports' with no sign of that.

overclaims: Microsoft nevertheless published useful explanations and implemented safeguards.
checks.note: The excerpt, the proposition with its Bing-scoped reading, the axis and the outcome match the case. e1 and e2 support the opacity point and the indirect prompt injection on deployed Bing/Edge within the window. Problems: the public evidence excerpts are cut to fragments ('Full details', 'succumbs', 'responsible AI') and do not state the items' quoted words. 'Useful' is an evaluative judgement that e3 does not support; e3 shows only that Microsoft described its approach and used classifiers. Optional: also note that the exploit was not retested on June 8.
